Quarterly Performance Report
Executive Summary & Analysis
This report presents the quarterly sales performance for the fiscal year 2024-25 across five product
categories: Soap, Hand Wash, Body Wash, Shampoo, and Face Wash. The year was marked by significant
volatility driven by external supply-chain factors and seasonal demand patterns. Reason 1 - Festive Season Demand (Q3-Q4): The festive season spanning Diwali in Q3 and the year-end
celebrations in Q4 drove a sharp increase in demand across all categories. Soap sales rose from 12,000
boxes in Q1 to 18,500 boxes in Q4, a 54% increase. Body Wash similarly jumped from 10,000 to 15,200
boxes. The festive period is traditionally the strongest sales window for personal care products in the Indian
wholesale market, as retailers stock up in anticipation of higher consumer spending on grooming and gifting. Reason 2 - Supplier Delay in Q2 (Distributor B): Q2 saw a noticeable dip across all categories. Distributor
B experienced logistics and customs delays that reduced supply by approximately 20-25% for two key product
lines.

Soap fell from 12,000 boxes in Q1 to 9,500 in Q2, and Shampoo dropped from 11,000 to 9,000. The
supply gap was resolved by Q3 as alternative sourcing arrangements were put in place. Reason 3 - Price Increase in Q4 (8-12% on Bar Soaps): A price revision was implemented in Q4, increasing
bar soap prices by 8-12% due to rising raw material costs. Despite the price increase, volume continued to
grow due to festive demand, resulting in higher revenue. The price change contributed to an estimated 15%
revenue uplift on soap alone. Face Wash, which had a smaller price adjustment of 5%, saw the most modest
Q4 increase, going from 6,000 boxes in Q1 to 8,500 in Q4.
